pass_a_gloss: And you will tread on the basilisk. Verse 10: But indeed, look, wild beasts are beside you. Of the same [author]: Beside you, Job; beside every one who remembers; beside everyone who has conquered. Verse 10: He eats grass like oxen. He means the worms that eat him from himself. For consummation, he says, my hand under you; and look, it eats as grass. Verse 11: And his power is upon the navel of the belly. This is the first power against the man. From here he begins to make fornication. Of the same: so that he may indicate the female, so that he may show that he campaigns not only against those who have the seeds. And very fittingly he named loin for the male, and navel of belly for the woman: Look, the strength of his loin is in strength; and his power is upon the navel of the belly. 17.101 Verse 25: And Phoenician nations divide it. Since the Canaanites, who are also Phoenicians, are accused of great wickedness, for this he says: Phoenician nations will divide him. Each takes some part from the dragon, if he is by race Canaanite and Phoenician. Verse 20?: And every floating thing coming together will not carry one hide of his tail. The last and extreme parts of the dragon all floating things together cannot kill. Human beings, using their bodies as boats, cannot carry one hide of his tail. By themselves they cannot; but when divine power oversees, we can not only carry one hide of his tail, but also bring the whole of him and kill the whole of him. And each kills, as far as is in him, the devil, according to what is said by the Apostle: May God crush Satan under your feet swiftly. Chapter 41 verse 4: Who will uncover the face of his clothing? Why did he not say: Who will uncover his face? What does clothing also do here? For who, he says, will uncover the face of his clothing? So that what is said may be understood, let us use the example of those who put on masks and do not appear as what they are, but want to seem [otherwise]. For they take up masks, for example,
pass_b_english: And you will tread on the basilisk. "[[But look — wild beasts are beside you >> Bible:Job 40:10]]." Beside you, Job; beside every one who keeps the memory; beside everyone who has won.

"[[He eats grass like oxen >> Bible:Job 40:10]]." Origen hears the worms that devour Job from his own flesh: a finishing stroke, he says, and "look, it eats as grass." "[[His power is upon the navel of the belly >> Bible:Job 40:11]]" — the first force set against the man, and the starting point of fornication. The same note marks the female so the campaign is not only against those who carry seed. Fittingly Scripture names the loin for the male and the navel of the belly for the woman: strength in the loin; power at the navel.

"[[Phoenician nations divide it >> Bible:Job 40:25]]." Because Canaanites — also called Phoenicians — are charged with great wickedness, each of that race takes a share from the dragon. "[[All the ships together cannot carry one hide of his tail >> Bible:Job 40:20]]": the dragon’s last extremities no fleet can kill. Humans sail in bodies as in boats and cannot lift even one hide of that tail by themselves; under divine oversight we can carry not only the hide but the whole beast and put it to death. Each kills the devil as far as lies in him, as the Apostle says: "[[May God crush Satan under your feet soon >> Bible:Romans 16:20]]."

Chapter 41: "[[Who will uncover the face of his clothing? >> Bible:Job 41:4]]" Why not simply "his face"? What is the clothing doing here? Take actors who put on masks and hide what they are so they may seem something else. They take up masks, for example—
